component.name: Mouse Without Borders
component.summary: Share input, clipboard, and files across Linux and Windows PCs

description.p: An independent Linux implementation and adaptation of PowerToys Mouse Without Borders. It connects Linux and Windows PCs using the native encrypted protocol and shares keyboard, pointer, text and PNG clipboard input, and cross-screen file drag-and-drop.
Wayland input uses the desktop InputCapture and RemoteDesktop portals, so the compositor remains in control and no root input helper is used.

Add encrypted cross-screen file drag-and-drop in both directions, reveal auto-hidden Linux docks from remotely controlled pointers, and keep connected Linux sessions available for remote wake with forced-suspend reconnection and portal recovery.
Make top-bar Exit fully shut down input capture and every background component without blocking GNOME Shell, and add DEB, RPM, and AppImage packages for x86-64 and ARM64.

Make the top-bar Exit action stop every sharing path while retaining only a disabled portal authorization session, and reuse that session without another permission prompt when the application is relaunched.

Recover connections automatically after suspend, retain approved input capture across UI relaunches, add Wake-on-LAN and lock-screen wake packets, and complete bidirectional Windows-hosted input and edge routing.
Add silent background update checks, update controls in Settings, verified GitHub release downloads, automatic Debian package installation, and relaunch only after the new version is installed.
Add an Ubuntu top-bar indicator with Open, Settings, and Exit actions. Closing the settings window now keeps Mouse Without Borders running in the background until Exit is selected from the indicator.

Add the four-computer matrix, concurrent multi-PC connections, directed input routing, multi-edge portal capture, four machine shortcuts, full bottom-edge pointer reach, and background-launch isolation for clipboard helpers.
Add compatibility with the final standalone Windows release, connect the settings controls to the live service, and reuse approved portal sessions across network reconnects.

Rebuild the settings window as the classic Mouse without Borders form, and draw the computer matrix from the monitors this computer really has so the thumbnail layout picks the screen edge that hands the pointer to the other computer.
Make connection listener restarts immediate and race-free.
Use the packaged systemd user service when the settings UI starts.
